_comment: Where the map coordinates come from, and which of the wiki's maps is real.
The wiki runs the DataMaps extension, so its maps are JSON pages in the
`Map:` namespace rather than pictures. Twelve exist. Exactly one is usable.
WHY ONLY ONE. The per-region pages — Map:Town, Map:Beach (Demo), Map:Narrows
(Demo), Map:The Summit, Map:Western Ruins, Map:Eastern Road (Demo),
Map:Hayden's Farm (Demo) — hold zero markers, and their declared coordinate
space does not match their own background: Map:Town claims 1074x2034 for a
1356x716 image. That is boilerplate someone pasted and never filled in.
Reading it would produce confident nonsense at a plausible-looking scale.
Map:V0.13 (Unlocked) is the opposite. Its space is 3599x5442 and its
background is 5442x3599 — the same numbers in the extension's [lat, lon]
order — and all 46 markers fall inside it. The enricher re-checks that
agreement on every run rather than trusting this comment.
Unlocked rather than Locked: the locked map hides five late-game markers,
and a place you cannot reach yet is shown and tagged, never hidden.
THE VERSION CAVEAT. This map is drawn for v0.13 and the game is 1.0. Things
may have moved. The map screen says so once, in one line; individual pins
are not each hedged, because a caveat repeated 46 times stops being read.
The hollow-pin treatment stays reserved for genuine inference — habitat
expansion — which this is not: these coordinates are published data.
The `article` field on each marker is the wiki page it links to, which is
the same page-name join every other enricher here already uses.
